chair.growth_thesis: YLapiano's Four Fits line up around one wedge: every credible competitor (Simply Piano, Yousician, Flowkey) is a $60-170/yr English-centric subscription, so 'real piano, songs in your language, €1 once, no ads, no data collected' is genuine Market-Product fit for subscription-fatigued parents. Channel-Model fit dictates everything else: €0.85 net can never fund paid UA (~$1.41 casual iOS CPI), so the only channels are App Store search, ratings compounding, and niche parenting communities (Turkish, Catalan) — which makes the store listing the acquisition loop and the rating average the growth engine. At this price the Model-Market constraint inverts the usual playbook: nobody refunds €1 over value, they refund and 1-star over 'broken' or 'prototype' — so refund/1-star prevention in the first 5 minutes IS the growth strategy, not D30 retention. Product-Channel fit means screenshots can only show what the median buyer reaches in minute one; today the shipping build seeds exactly ONE song and the mic promise is dead code, so completeness work (catalog, persistence, uniform game mode, honest input claims) precedes any store work. Win condition: 4.5+ stars at 10-15 ratings in TR week one, then EU expansion rides the same listing.
chair.activation_metric: Setup moment: parent completes an input proof-of-life during onboarding (app names a note the kid plays via mic, or USB MIDI connects). Aha moment: the kid's first DELIBERATE correct-key hit on the real instrument with instant audiovisual response (glow + sparkle + sound), within 90 seconds of device handover, zero adult words. Activated household: in session 1 the kid finishes one song to the stars+Pim result screen, and at next launch the home screen shows their persisted stars (proves the app 'remembered'). Measurement (no analytics, by design): pre-launch = cold-open playtest gate (>=4/5 kids reach aha <90s; >=3/5 day-3 unprompted reopen); post-launch proxies = App Store Connect refund count and rating average >=4.5.

decisions.question: Onboarding/FTUE — what's the right v1 for a pre-reader kid + parent setup?
decisions.decision: Kill the 3 text pages. v1 = exactly two beats: (1) ONE illustrated parent setup page — device-on-piano placement illustration, mic-vs-USB-MIDI choice, mic pre-prompt, ending in a live proof-of-life ('play any key' — app names the note it heard, with a didn't-hear-it fallback panel); (2) the kid plays immediately — Pim points at a glowing key, a 3-note tutorial runs through the existing song-agnostic FallingNotesScene at rung-1 forgiveness (slow, full glow, ±600ms), flowing straight into the easiest song. No 'you're all set' page, no separate tutorial engine, zero reading required of the kid.
decisions.rationale: All 9 personas converged on 'kill the text pages, make the kid's first 60 seconds the core verb.' The apparent conflict (Luca/Khalid/Market's mic magic-moment vs Defne/Mei's playable kid moment) dissolves — they are the same flow, parent beat then kid beat. Marco verified FallingNotesScene is fully song-agnostic, so this is routing + assets, not an engine. The live input check converts the #1 refund driver ('it doesn't hear my piano') into the first wow moment.

decisions.question: Microphone input (cross-cutting conflict: Mei says delete it, Luca/Marco/Market say showcase it)
decisions.decision: Wire the mic for real, with a kill criterion. Route PitchDetector.detectedNote into the same game-mode hit-judging path as key presses (Marco verified it only drives the legacy sheet-music loop today and startListening() is never called — Mei is factually right that it's currently a dead promise). Then gate it behind the onboarding proof-of-life check. Kill criterion: if mic judging fails the on-device acoustic-piano test before submission, execute Mei's plan — strip the mic permission page and ALL 'hears your piano' copy, and ship honestly as touch + USB MIDI.
decisions.rationale: Touch-only guts the 'real piano' wedge the entire market positioning rests on, so the upside justifies the M-effort attempt. But the one unacceptable state is the current one: requesting a permission for a feature that doesn't function — a justified-refund machine and an App Review smell. Either branch (working mic or honest removal) is shippable; the dishonest middle is not.

decisions.question: Song catalog & regional/language bundling
decisions.decision: All songs included for everyone — no packs, no IAP, no pick-your-language onboarding step. Structure: locale-aware sections on home ('Your songs' = device-locale matches first, then 'More songs'), sorted easy→hard WITHIN sections via a new difficultyRank. Launch blocker discovered: the shipping build seeds exactly ONE song (createSeedSongs returns [plimPlim()]); restore the 8 retired builders + add 4 Turkish songs (Mini Mini Bir Kuş, Ali Babanın Çiftliği, Yağ Satarım Bal Satarım, Kırmızı Balık) to hit 12-14, on top of the seedID identity refactor so seeding stops deleting user songs by title match. Localize song display titles per locale (Twinkle = 'Daha Dün Annemizin', Old MacDonald = 'Ali Baba'nın Çiftliği', Frère Jacques = 'Tembel Çocuk'). Completeness ruling: EVERY song launches falling-notes game mode and ends in the same stars+Pim result screen; the full 4-rung mastery ladder stays Salta-only for v1.
decisions.rationale: Unanimous do_not_do on packs/gating (notes are ~1-2KB; hidden songs make a €1 app feel thinner). Defne's difficulty ordering and the locale-sort camp aren't in conflict — sections by locale, ladder within. On gamification depth, Mei/Defne's 'uniform result is the completeness fix' overrules Luca's L-effort full-ladder rollout: thinness comes from 8 of 9 songs ending in a flat text overlay, not from missing rungs, and screenshots must show what every song actually does. Turkey-first with zero Turkish songs was the single most-repeated refund risk across personas.

decisions.question: Pim presence — where does the mascot live, cheap-but-effective?
decisions.decision: Re-anchor canon to CHIBI (overruling the pim-reward-assets skill's painterly declaration): one OpenArt session producing a new chibi app icon + 3-4 static stills — greeting (home header), pointing (FTUE guide), listening (mic states), and the missing MascotCheer (referenced at PlayerScreen.swift:592, absent from Assets). Retire Mascot.png (the third squirrel). Add Khalid's 5-6 wordless squirrel chirps (.caf, adult voice pitched up — never ElevenLabs child voices) layered over the silent reward videos, onboarding, and home greeting. Pim lives in exactly four places: icon, home header, onboarding, result screen. No Lottie/Rive/Spine, no new videos, no rig.
decisions.rationale: Aiko's chibi re-anchor is the cheap direction (new icon = 1 still; matching the videos to painterly = 3 fragile regenerations) and chibi wins the 60x60 thumbnail test. Three squirrels reads as asset-flip carelessness — the icon writes a check the app must cash. Mei's research point seals the budget: kids attach through repetition of the SAME pose, not animation everywhere. Diego's idle video loop (reusing the shipped chroma-key player) is a stretch inside the motion pass, not a gate.

decisions.question: Home screen redesign — what does 'designed' mean at minimal cost?
decisions.decision: Keep the LazyVGrid — the problem is missing DATA, not design tech. 'Designed' = (1) persisted best-stars row on every card + rung badge (requires the persistence item — today rungIndex dies on every launch), (2) chibi Pim greeting in a warm header band replacing the system-white nav, (3) locale sections, (4) per-song picture icons so a pre-reader can find 'their' song, (5) Theme.swift palette tokens (<=12 colors), (6) Add Song demoted to a parental-gated toolbar '+' and long-press delete removed from kid reach, (7) Diego's press-squash + staggered entrance. Acceptance test (Luca's): does this screen survive as App Store frame #1 next to Pok Pok?
decisions.rationale: Six personas independently named stars-on-cards as the single biggest completeness signal — it converts '9 songs' into '36+ visible challenges' and gives day-3 reopens a target. The ungated long-press delete is simultaneously a refund bomb (kid erases the catalog in one gesture) and a parental-gate requirement. No hero illustrations, no metagame map — it's a catalog browser for ~13 songs.

decisions.question: Store readiness — what must be true in-app before screenshot day?
decisions.decision: Gates: (1) catalog restored to 12+ with Turkish songs and ear-verified notes (incl. the Salta Sol-vs-Mi flag), (2) progress persists and shows on home, (3) every song ends in the same stars+Pim result, (4) playable FTUE shipped, (5) one squirrel everywhere, (6) TR strings ACTUALLY in the build — migrate to a String Catalog; the existing en/es .lproj files are not in the resources build phase, so zero localization ships today, (7) compliance pack done: privacy policy URL (currently missing, hard blocker), Data Not Collected label, localized NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, App Review notes pre-empting the mic-with-kids question. Kids Category ruling: NO for v1 — file at 4+ instead (ASO overrules Luca). iPad-only stays; fix store-config.md's incorrect iPhone 6.7" frame plan (build is TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY=2). Frame arc: 4 frames — falling-notes hero, hears-your-real-piano, Pim celebration, library-with-stars — plus a trust frame ('no ads · no subscriptions · no data collected'), tr + en-US only, via a deterministic -screenshotState seed mechanism.
decisions.rationale: Kids Category is a one-way door, mic access inside it triggers extended review, and the Kids tab skews free — the worst trade for a solo dev racing a submission; Luca's trust story survives intact without enrollment since 'Data Not Collected' is verifiably true (no network/analytics code exists). Screenshots-last is the core anti-refund principle: every frame must show a state the buyer reaches in minute one.

decisions.question: Launch — how to ship without chasing perfection?
decisions.decision: Three-stage organic launch, zero paid UA, no metrics theater. Go/no-go gate = Mei's cold-open playtest (5 age-5 kids, not Deniz: >=4/5 reach a deliberate correct hit <90s unprompted; >=3/5 day-3 reopen — recruit families NOW, they're the long pole) + one clean TestFlight device week on the restored catalog + the compliance pack. Stage 1: quiet TR-only submission as a crash/refund/review shakeout and a 10-15-honest-ratings sprint from TR friends + the Catalan circle (TR metrics run low — never read them as global signal). Stage 2 (after ~7-14 days + one fix release): EN storefronts + EU in one release; first real marketing beat is the Catalan niche ('Sol Solet on a real piano' to criança-en-català communities) — genuinely rare content, warmest audience. Stage 3: TR community push (Turkish songs are in at launch via the catalog item). Apple Featuring nomination on every release + Common Sense Media submission as upside, never the plan. Scoreboard: App Store Connect refund count + rating average. Do NOT gate on: mascot animation, full ladders on all songs, App Preview video, es/ca listings, or any cohort table you'll never have at solo-€1 volume.
decisions.rationale: At €1 the bar is 'no buyer's remorse in the first 5 minutes,' not retention curves; reviews ARE the kid data at this volume. Launch is the playtest at scale, so the pre-launch playtest is the only gate that predicts it. Sequencing puts the cheapest-to-absorb market first and saves each marketing beat for when its content claim is true.

tech_risks: B5 mic judging may simply not work on an acoustic piano: the autocorrelation detector is mono-pitch and piano harmonics/sustain/speaker-bleed under .playAndRecord will confuse it — treat the 4-day estimate as capped by the kill criterion and have the strip-the-mic branch (Mei) genuinely ready, not theoretical.

B2's dotted-notes-and-rests change mutates the Codable schema inside Song.notesData — existing user-created songs from build 6 must still decode after update; pair it with B1 and test the upgrade path on a device carrying real data, because data-loss-on-update is the refund class this whole backlog exists to prevent.

Seed migration (B1) is upgrade-path sensitive: the title→seedID adoption must run exactly once against a store created by the shipped build, or you get duplicate/deleted songs; fresh-install testing alone will pass and lie to you.

B5 and B6 interact: switching the unified session to .playAndRecord changes output routing and levels (receiver vs speaker, ducking) for the piano sampler that currently runs under .playback — verify game audio volume and latency on a real iPad after the category change, not just that the mic works.

The Xcode project uses manual file references, so every new file (Theme.swift, MotionTokens.swift, gate component, xcstrings) is a pbxproj edit — batch file additions per PR or Claude will burn time on project-file merge noise across B9/B13/B16.

rice.notes:
Method: RICE per jpm-prioritization SKILL.md; RICE = (Reach% x Impact x Confidence) / effort_days. Reach = % of buyer households touched in first/week-1 sessions; first cohort installs fresh, so anything on the first-session path (catalog, FTUE, player, listing) is 100. Goal lens: refund prevention (parent's 2-min judgment) + kid replay (day-2 return).

Tier logic, not pure RICE rank: NOW = anything whose absence is a refund-shaped hole at launch or a hard submission blocker. B5 scores low (48) because of 4-day effort and 0.8 confidence (acoustic-piano detection risk) but stays NOW — it is the core 'real piano' promise and the built-in kill criterion (strip mic honestly) caps the downside; treat the Mei strip-the-mic branch as the schedule backstop. B2 also under-indexes on RICE (effort 3) but one-song catalog is the minute-one refund; non-negotiable NOW. B22 is the go/no-go gate — start family recruiting immediately since it is calendar time, not effort.

NOW totals ~27.5 effort days. Dependency-safe order: B1 -> B3 -> B6 -> B2 -> B4 -> B5 (kill decision) -> B7 -> B13 -> B10 -> B9 -> B11 -> B8 -> B18 -> B19 -> B20 -> B21 -> B22 (sessions). Store items (B18-B21) are deliberately last so screenshots show truth.

NEXT (v1.x fast-follow): B12, B14, B15 deepen the kid bond/replay loop but no parent refunds over their absence in week 1; B17 scores lowest (32) — keep it NEXT but fold the bare support mailto into B18's privacy page now so a week-1 'broken' email path exists before the full Grown-Ups corner ships. LATER: B16 (juice polish, reduced-motion items in it that are reviewer-visible can ride along with B8/B9 touches). CUT: none — this backlog was already committee-curated; nothing here is speculative scope.

Quick-wins-trap check per skill guardrails: distribution is healthy — the big bets (B2, B5, B8) sit in NOW alongside the quick wins; no avoided strategic initiative.

Confidence flags: B5 (0.8, device-test outcome unknown), B8 (0.8, kid moment needs on-device iteration), B22 (0.8, recruiting risk). Everything verified-in-code (B6 mute bug, B3 progress wipe, B5 dead startListening, B7 missing MascotCheer) scored 1.0.

cuts.reason: Home-card previews are charming but sit outside the refund window — a parent doesn't refund over missing previews, and B14's picture icons solve pre-reader song-finding for a third of the cost. Parked, not killed: revisit trigger = post-launch review mentioning 'can't find songs'.

Motion pass is polish on screens that don't yet have their data (stars, sections) — juice on an unfinished home is paint on wet plaster. B9 already carries the press-squash and staggered entrance the chair mandated; the full MotionTokens system + reduced-motion audit + PimIdle stretch parks until v1.1. Revisit trigger = first post-launch release.

Explicitly re-killing the stretch inside the parked item so it doesn't sneak back: no new Pim videos, no LoopingVideoView extraction before launch. Chair already ruled it 'a stretch, not a gate' — at 7.5 weeks total there is no stretch budget.

kill_criteria: Mic kill (end of Phase 2): if pitch detection cannot judge hits on a real acoustic piano in the on-device test, strip the mic permission page and ALL 'hears your piano' copy and ship touch + USB MIDI. The current dead-permission state never reaches review.

Playtest kill (Phase 4 gate): fewer than 4/5 kids reach a deliberate correct hit under 90 seconds unprompted, or fewer than 3/5 reopen by day 3 → do NOT submit. Fix forgiveness/FTUE, re-run with 2-3 fresh kids. Two consecutive failed gates = stop and rethink the core loop, not the schedule.

Data-loss hard stop: if the B1 migration or any later schema change loses user songs or progress on upgrade from build 6, the release is blocked until fixed. No exceptions — data loss is the worst refund class on the board.

Schedule kill (end of week 5): if Phases 1-2 aren't both exited, cut B14 + B12 + B17 in that order and ship the core (catalog + persistence + FTUE + home + TR strings). The submission date moves last.

Post-launch kill (Stage 1 watch): refund count trending above ~1 in 10 sales or rating average below 4.0 on the TR storefront in the first 14 days → halt the EN/EU rollout, ship the fix release first. TR metrics are never read as global signal in either direction.
launch_steps: 1. TestFlight: push the Phase-3 build (full catalog, FTUE, home, TR strings) to Onur's devices + 2-3 friend families; start the one clean device week.
2. Playtest gate: run the 5-kid cold-open sessions (B22 criteria) on that build; day-3 reopen check; GO/NO-GO decision recorded in product/decisions/.
3. Fix release: one small TestFlight iteration from playtest findings (timing windows, FTUE stalls) — small fixes only, no new features past the gate.

4. Store assets: B20 deterministic states → B21 screenshot kit (tr + en-US, iPad 13" only) + B19 metadata uploaded; verify privacy URL, nutrition label 'Data Not Collected', 4+ rating answers, mic App Review notes.
5. Submit Stage 1: TR storefront ONLY. Quiet shakeout — no marketing beat. Apple Featuring nomination filed with the release.
6. Stage 1 watch (days 1-14): daily App Store Connect check — refund count + rating average, nothing else. Sprint to 10-15 honest ratings from TR friends + the Catalan circle. Ship one fix release.

7. Stage 2 (after ~7-14 days + the fix release): EN storefronts + EU in one release. First real marketing beat: 'Sol Solet on a real piano' to criança-en-català communities — the warmest audience, saved for when the claim is live.
8. Stage 3: TR community push (Turkish songs already in since Phase 1). Common Sense Media submission filed as upside, never the plan.

9. First-week watch routine per stage: reply to every review, route 'it doesn't hear my piano' to the Grown-Ups support mailto, log refund reasons. Scoreboard stays two numbers: refunds + rating average. No cohort tables at solo-€1 volume.
